item.text:
I did not assign a score.

**Orientation**
- AMLO had direct control over the federal budget, social transfers, state-owned enterprises, and major infrastructure choices in 2022, while Banxico, CONEVAL, COFECE, and ASF remained important institutional checks.
- The 2022 backdrop was mixed: post-pandemic recovery, U.S. demand, Russia-Ukraine spillovers, and a severe inflation shock. Independent sources consistently show macro stability was broadly preserved, but investment, competition, and flagship-project execution were weak or contested.
- On attribution, the strongest AMLO-linked evidence in 2022 is about fiscal priorities, energy-market intervention, social transfers, and project selection. Inflation and monetary tightening were mostly institutional responses rather than presidential control.

**Evidence Index**
- [IMF 2022 Article IV Consultation](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2022/11/04/mexico-2022-article-iv-consultation-press-release-and-staff-report-525448): neutral fiscal stance, largely untargeted subsidies, inflation surge, debt and reserves.
- [OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2022/02/oecd-economic-surveys-mexico-2022_a2937d37.html): weak long-run growth, informality, weak competition, low investment, corruption and regulatory uncertainty.
- [Banxico monetary policy announcements](https://www.banxico.org.mx/publicaciones-y-prensa/anuncios-de-las-decisiones-de-politica-monetaria/anuncios-politica-monetaria-t.html): repeated 2022 hikes into double digits.
- [INEGI CPI June 2022](https://en.www.inegi.org.mx/app/saladeprensa/noticia.html?id=7441): inflation at 7.99% in June.
- [CONEVAL labor poverty Q4 2022](https://www.coneval.org.mx/Medicion/Paginas/Pobreza_laboral_4toTrim2022.aspx): labor poverty fell but stayed high.
- [CONEVAL multidimensional poverty 2022](https://www.coneval.org.mx/InformesPublicaciones/Paginas/Mosaicos/Informe_Pobreza_Multidimensional_2022.aspx): 36.3% poverty, 7.1% extreme poverty.
- [CONASAMI minimum wage 2022](https://www.gob.mx/conasami/articulos/incremento-a-los-salarios-minimos-para-2022?idiom=es): 22% minimum-wage increase.
- [Cuenta Pública 2022](https://www.transparenciapresupuestaria.gob.mx/es/PTP/Cuenta_Publica_2022): large social, pension, and investment outlays.
- [Reuters on Dos Bocas cost escalation](https://m.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/mexicos-pemex-requests-65-billion-more-funding-for-dos-bocas-refinery--documents-source-2871661?ampMode=1): cost overruns on the signature refinery.
- [Reuters on electricity overhaul defeat](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/mexican-lawmakers-to-vote-on-presidents-contentious-electricity-overhaul-2804968): market and trade concerns, reform failure.
- [COFECE first-quarter 2022 report](https://www.cofece.mx/cofece-entrega-su-primer-informa-trimestral-de-actividades-2022/): enforcement actions and a major airport fine.
- [SHCP anti-inflation accord](https://www.gob.mx/shcp/prensa/comunicado-no-67-gobierno-federal-y-empresas-productoras-y-distribuidoras-acuerdan-diversas-medidas-contra-la-inflacion): PACIC-style basket-price measures.
- [ASF Tren Maya anomaly reporting](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2022/02/20/politica/asf-detecta-anomalias-por-mas-de-mil-44-mdp-en-obras-de-tren-maya-7020): audit irregularities in a flagship project.
- [Senate transcript on Victoria Rodriguez Ceja](https://comunicacionsocial.senado.gob.mx/informacion/prensa/5780-version-estenografica-de-la-comparecencia-de-): appointment and qualifications.
- [Reuters factbox on Victoria Rodriguez Ceja](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/factboxvictoria-rodriguez-mexicos-new-pick-for-central-bank-governor-2689873): investor concern about politicization.

**Lens Disposition**
| Lens | Disposition | Main evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 5B.1 Broad and sustainable prosperity | Mixed to adverse | IMF, OECD, budget, min-wage policy, energy-policy conflict |
| 5B.2 Qualified economic leadership | Mixed | Senate biography/ratification vs Reuters market concerns |
| 5B.3 Macroeconomic stability | Mixed positive | IMF, Banxico hikes, INEGI inflation |
| 5B.4 Fair economic rules | Mixed to adverse | OECD, electricity reform defeat, COFECE enforcement |
| 5B.5 Resistance to capture | Mixed to adverse | Energy-market dispute, project overruns, COFECE/ASF oversight |
| 5B.6 Productive public investment | Mixed to adverse | Cuenta Pública, Dos Bocas, ASF/Tren Maya |
| 5B.7 Evidence and correction | Mixed | SHCP anti-inflation response, IMF critique of untargeted subsidies |
| 5B.8 Fair distribution | Mixed | Minimum wage, labor poverty, multidimensional poverty, social spending |
| 5B.9 Managing economic shocks | Mixed | Inflation shock response, PACIC, Banxico tightening |
| 5B.10 Lasting economic trajectory | Mixed to adverse | OECD structural constraints, poverty/informality, weak investment |

**Source Groups**
- Accepted evidence: IMF Article IV, OECD survey, Banxico policy table, INEGI CPI, CONEVAL labor poverty, CONEVAL multidimensional poverty, CONASAMI wage increase, Cuenta Pública 2022, Dos Bocas Reuters report, electricity reform Reuters report, COFECE Q1 report, SHCP anti-inflation communiqué, ASF/Tren Maya reporting, Senate transcript.
- Corroborating context: Reuters factbox on Banxico appointment, IMF notes on untargeted subsidies, OECD remarks on competition and informality.
- Discovery-only leads not fully developed here: [ASF 2022 audit index](https://www.asf.gob.mx/Trans/Informes/IR2022c/index.html), [Banxico quarterly reports index](https://www.banxico.org.mx/publications-and-press/quarterly-reports/quarterly-reports-prices-banc.html), [World Bank Mexico Macro Poverty Outlook 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659110162429895).

**Counts and Gaps**
- Developed records: 15
- High-confidence official sources: 10
- Secondary corroboration/context sources: 5
- Main remaining gaps: granular distribution by region and household type, direct causal attribution of 2022 inflation and growth to AMLO versus external shocks, and full original ASF audit findings for the flagship projects beyond coverage/index or media summaries.

SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"EL CONEVAL PRESENTA INFORMACION REFERENTE A LA POBREZA LABORAL AL CUARTO TRIMESTRE DE 2022","publisher":"CONEVAL","publication_date":"2023-02","url":"https://www.coneval.org.mx/Medicion/Paginas/Pobreza_laboral_4toTrim2022.aspx","claim":"CONEVAL reported that labor poverty fell to 38.5% in Q4 2022 from 40.3% in Q4 2021, while real per-capita labor income rose 4.3% year over year, but the level remained above the pre-pandemic benchmark.","locator":"Headline bullets and body text","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-007","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_labor_poverty_and_income","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"source_type":"official_statistics","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary social-statistics release tied to INEGI labor data.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"later-retrospective","ruler_attribution":"Only partly attributable to AMLO; labor-market recovery, transfers, and wage policy mattered, but so did post-pandemic rebound and inflation.","contrary_evidence":"The improvement did not return the indicator to pre-pandemic levels and the rural/urban gap stayed large.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_labor_poverty_recovery","lenses":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Informe de la pobreza multidimensional en Mexico, 2022","publisher":"CONEVAL","publication_date":"2025-01","url":"https://www.coneval.org.mx/InformesPublicaciones/Paginas/Mosaicos/Informe_Pobreza_Multidimensional_2022.aspx","claim":"CONEVAL's 2022 poverty report says 46.8 million people, or 36.3% of Mexico's population, were in multidimensional poverty in 2022, including 9.1 million, or 7.1%, in extreme poverty.","locator":"Report summary","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-008","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_multidimensional_poverty","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.8","5B.10"],"source_type":"official_statistics","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official retrospective poverty measurement based on ENIGH 2022.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"later-retrospective","ruler_attribution":"Only partly attributable to AMLO because the measure reflects inherited inequality, labor conditions, transfers, inflation, and recovery effects.","contrary_evidence":"The same report also shows substantial poverty reduction versus 2018, so the direction is not uniformly negative.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_multidimensional_poverty","lenses":["5B.8","5B.10"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Incremento a los Salarios Minimos para 2022","publisher":"Comision Nacional de los Salarios Minimos","publication_date":"2021-12-01","url":"https://www.gob.mx/conasami/articulos/incremento-a-los-salarios-minimos-para-2022?idiom=es","claim":"Mexico's 2022 minimum wage rose 22%, from 141.70 to 172.87 pesos per day in the general zone and from 213.39 to 260.34 pesos in the northern border zone.","locator":"Policy announcement text","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-009","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_minimum_wage_increase","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9"],"source_type":"official_policy","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary wage-setting announcement from the responsible federal commission.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"target-year","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's labor-policy agenda and the tripartite wage-setting process under his administration.","contrary_evidence":"A wage hike supports incomes, but it does not by itself prove broad-based sustainable prosperity if inflation and informality remain high.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_minimum_wage_policy","lenses":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Cuenta Publica 2022","publisher":"Transparencia Presupuestaria / SHCP","publication_date":"2023","url":"https://www.transparenciapresupuestaria.gob.mx/es/PTP/Cuenta_Publica_2022","claim":"Mexico's 2022 public accounts show total public spending of 7.595 trillion pesos, including 3.464 trillion for social development, 1.256 trillion for investment, 917 billion for physical investment, and 1.184 trillion for pensions and retirements.","locator":"Expenditure summary tables","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-010","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_public_spending_structure","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8"],"source_type":"official_budget","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official public accounts data from the federal transparency portal.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"target-year","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's budget priorities, though execution also reflected administrative and congressional constraints.","contrary_evidence":"The spending envelope was large, but the category totals alone do not establish project quality or distributional efficiency.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_budget_social_investment_spending","lenses":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico's Pemex requests $6.5 billion more funding for 'Dos Bocas' refinery -documents, source","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-08-12","url":"https://m.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/mexicos-pemex-requests-65-billion-more-funding-for-dos-bocas-refinery--documents-source-2871661?ampMode=1","claim":"Reuters reported that Pemex sought almost $6.5 billion more for the Dos Bocas refinery, lifting the project estimate to $14.6 billion from an original $8.9 billion, with $10.3 billion already spent by June 2022.","locator":"Lead and cost summary","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-011","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_dos_bocas_cost_escalation","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.6","5B.5"],"source_type":"press","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters-based reporting on documents and sources, but still secondary to the underlying budget and procurement records.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"target-year","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's signature-energy-project choices.","contrary_evidence":"The administration framed the refinery as energy sovereignty and import substitution, but the cost escalation is still material evidence of execution risk.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_dos_bocas_overrun","lenses":["5B.6","5B.5"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexican president's contentious electricity overhaul defeated in Congress","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-04-17","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/mexican-lawmakers-to-vote-on-presidents-contentious-electricity-overhaul-2804968","claim":"Reuters reported that Congress defeated AMLO's electricity overhaul, which would have given the state utility priority over private generators, lifted the CFE's share toward 54%, and weakened independent regulators; critics said it would hurt investment and breach trade obligations.","locator":"Lead and vote summary","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-012","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_electricity_reform_failure","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.5"],"source_type":"press","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters is reliable for the legislative outcome and contemporaneous criticism, but it remains secondary reporting.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"target-year","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's legislative agenda and policy preferences.","contrary_evidence":"The bill's defeat shows institutional resistance and limits on presidential control, so the policy did not fully convert into law.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_electricity_reform_rejected","lenses":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.5"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Cofece entrega a los Poderes Ejecutivo y Legislativo su Primer Informa Trimestral de Actividades 2022","publisher":"Comision Federal de Competencia Economica","publication_date":"2022-04-28","url":"https://www.cofece.mx/cofece-entrega-su-primer-informa-trimestral-de-actividades-2022/","claim":"COFECE said it analyzed 85 concentrations in the first quarter of 2022 and imposed a 848,888,633-peso fine on AICM for denying and favoring access in passenger ground-transport services, showing active competition enforcement.","locator":"Bullet list of results","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-013","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_cofece_enforcement_activity","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.4","5B.5"],"source_type":"official_regulator","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary competition-authority report with concrete enforcement actions and amounts.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"target-year","ruler_attribution":"Indirectly attributable: it shows the state of competition enforcement under AMLO, not a direct presidential decision.","contrary_evidence":"The existence of enforcement does not prove that capture or weak competition were solved; OECD still described structural weaknesses.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_cofece_enforcement","lenses":["5B.4","5B.5"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Comunicado No. 67 Gobierno Federal y empresas productoras y distribuidoras acuerdan diversas medidas contra la inflacion","publisher":"Secretaria de Hacienda y Credito Publico","publication_date":"2022-10-03","url":"https://www.gob.mx/shcp/prensa/comunicado-no-67-gobierno-federal-y-empresas-productoras-y-distribuidoras-acuerdan-diversas-medidas-contra-la-inflacion","claim":"The federal government and private firms agreed on complementary PACIC measures in October 2022, including a stated goal of reducing the average 24-item basic-basket ceiling by 8% from 1,129 to 1,039 pesos while continuing fuel and electricity price containment.","locator":"Communique summary bullets","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-014","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_2022_pacic_anti_inflation_measures","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.7","5B.8","5B.9"],"source_type":"official_policy","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary federal communiqué describing the anti-inflation package and its numeric target.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"target-year","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to AMLO's administration and economic team.","contrary_evidence":"The package targeted prices and supply, but IMF later judged fuel stabilization largely untargeted and costly.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_2022_pacic_response","lenses":["5B.7","5B.8","5B.9"]}
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"ASF detecta anomalias por mas de mil 44 mdp en obras de Tren Maya","publisher":"La Jornada","publication_date":"2022-02-20","url":"https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2022/02/20/politica/asf-detecta-anomalias-por-mas-de-mil-44-mdp-en-obras-de-tren-maya-7020","claim":"La Jornada reported that ASF found more than 1,044 million pesos in anomalies in Tren Maya works in the review of the 2020 public account, including undocumented or only partially documented payments and convention-based transfers to Fonatur-Tren Maya.","locator":"Lead and anomaly summary","provisional_id":"WEB-5B-015","canonical_fact_key":"mexico_tren_maya_audit_anomalies_2020_reported_2022","disposition":"final_evidence","chapter_ids":["5B"],"methodology_ids":["5B.5","5B.6"],"source_type":"press","source_confidence":"medium","source_confidence_reason":"The story reports official ASF findings, but it is still secondary coverage rather than the audit PDF itself.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"inherited_context","ruler_attribution":"Directly relevant to AMLO because Tren Maya was a flagship presidential project and the anomalies concern its execution and oversight.","contrary_evidence":"This is audit-coverage evidence rather than a final ruling on fraud or misuse, so the anomaly count should not be overread as proved corruption.","underlying_fact_key":"fact_mexico_tren_maya_audit_anomalies","lenses":["5B.5","5B.6"]}
